# Ephe accepted advisory risk register — every ecosystem the audits can see
#
# This file is INPUT, not prose: `.github/workflows/supply-chain.yml` reads the ID lines
# below and passes the PyPI ones to `pip-audit --ignore-vuln`. Everything else in the
# audit stays visible, so an ignored advisory is always a written decision and a new
# one is never silently tolerated. tests/test_supply_chain_gate.py holds the format, the
# state and the expiry of every entry, and scripts/advisory_id_check.py resolves each ID
# against the advisory databases before any of them counts as accepted.
#
# Line format:
#   <ID>  # package=<name> [ecosystem=<PyPI|npm|crates.io>] [scope=<runtime|development>]
#          [state=<accepted|pending-fix|fixed>] affected=<range> fixed_in=<version|none>
#          [blocked_by=<what is missing>] recheck=<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Omitted fields default to ecosystem=PyPI, state=accepted. The three states are the three
# homes a finding can have: `accepted` means no release exists and the risk is carried with
# a written exposure; `pending-fix` means a release exists, the move is somebody's open
# work, and `blocked_by=` names what is missing; `fixed` means the fix landed and the row
# stays as the floor that stops it returning, so `fixed_in=` names the version the lock must
# hold and `blocked_by=` is absent because nothing is missing. Only rows that are PyPI and
# `accepted` reach `--ignore-vuln`, so an npm or crates.io ID can never silence a Python
# finding, and a closed finding is never hidden by the flag that hides an open one.
# A line whose recheck date has passed makes the gate job fail, so a decision cannot
# outlive itself without somebody noticing. That holds for every state: a `pending-fix` row
# sitting past its date is the same silence as an `accepted` one, only slower.
#
# Measured 2026-10-14 against the locked set. multidict (GHSA-54p9-h82j-f925 =
# CVE-2026-104874) was FIXED and is held by `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies` in
# pyproject.toml; since 2026-10-14 it carries a `state=fixed` row below rather than only a
# comment, because a floor nobody restates is a floor the next `uv lock --upgrade` drops.
#
# Six rows left this register on 2026-10-14 with the packages they named. The reason stays
# written here instead of being a deletion with no trace:
#   * PYSEC-2026-311 / -3813 / -3814 / -3815 (chromadb) were `state=accepted fixed_in=none`
#     because the advisory ranges end at last_affected=1.5.9 and no release above it exists
#     to move to. The product left the package instead: `chromadb` is out of uv.lock and
#     pyproject.toml, so `uv export --frozen` no longer emits it and pip-audit can no longer
#     report it. An `accepted` row for a package the lock does not carry claims a risk we
#     do not hold.
#   * PYSEC-2026-4175 (urllib3) and PYSEC-2026-4114 (oauthlib) were `state=fixed` floors.
#     Both reached the product only as chromadb -> kubernetes -> {requests-oauthlib,
#     urllib3}, so both left the lock with chromadb, and their two constraints left
#     `[tool.uv]` in the same change. The gate reads every `fixed` row back against uv.lock,
#     so the row and the constraint had to move together.
# tests/test_supply_chain_gate.py holds both readings, including the empty `--ignore-flags`
# set this leaves behind: a row returning without its flag fails that job.

# aiohttp 3.14.3 carried three advisories: GHSA-2g87-pp6c-29x5 (unbounded
# memory/CPU), a shared-cookie Secure attribute, and the missing initial
# request/header timeout. The lock now holds 3.14.5; 3.14.4 is the first patched
# release for all three. aiohttp reaches Ephe through edge-tts, the optional
# voice path, as a client; the FastAPI server is uvicorn.
# Why it is fixed: uv.lock moved to 3.14.5 and the frozen resolver has no path
# back below it; pip-audit reports no aiohttp finding against the export.
# Exposure as measured: aiohttp reaches Ephe only through edge-tts, the
# optional voice path, as a client. The FastAPI server is uvicorn; the
# server-side vectors in the three advisories did not apply to that use, and
# the bump removes the finding for every install that carries the extra.
GHSA-2g87-pp6c-29x5  # package=aiohttp ecosystem=PyPI scope=runtime state=fixed affected=<=3.14.3 fixed_in=3.14.5 recheck=2026-11-06

# Re-check protocol for the entries below:
#   1. `/work/.local/bin/uv pip compile` is not used here; the authoritative
#      command is the one the gate runs — `uv export --frozen --all-groups --no-emit-project
#      --no-hashes` into a requirements file, then `pip-audit -r <file> --no-deps`.
#   2. A row moves to `state=fixed` when the bump lands and the audit stops reporting it,
#      and it stays with `fixed_in=` naming the version the lock must hold.
#   3. `state=fixed` describes a package the lock still carries. A floor whose package
#      leaves the product is removed with it, as the six rows above were, and the reason is
#      written down before the line goes.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# npm and crates.io — the surfaces `pip-audit` cannot see
#
# These lines are records, not pip-audit flags: `--ignore-flags` derives from rows that are
# PyPI, so an npm or crates.io ID can never silence a Python finding. They are still read by
# the resolver and by the expiry check like every other entry above.
#
# Why they are entries now and were prose before: the entry grammar accepted
# `PYSEC-2026-311` and rejected `GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7`, although ANY_ID in
# tests/test_supply_chain_gate.py already knew the GHSA shape and
# scripts/advisory_id_check.py already knew it too (its SHAPES table). A GHSA-shaped
# finding therefore had no legal line form in either register, and the seven JS advisories
# measured on 2026-10-09 were written as prose instead. Prose satisfies the
# docs-citation fence, which reads the raw file text, and escapes the expiry, the ID
# resolution and the flag derivation, which parse lines. Seven undated findings sat behind
# five days of green gates. The grammar in all three readers now accepts the GHSA shape and
# every line carries a state and a date.
#
# Measured 2026-10-14 in app/, with the gate's own commands:
#   pnpm audit --prod --json  -> 1 record, katex 0.16.47, dev=false
#   pnpm audit --json         -> 8 records, {low 1, moderate 2, high 5}
# The same day the bot's alert list and this register only partly overlapped: one
# advisory is counted once per locked version (brace-expansion 1.1.18 and 5.0.9 are two of
# them), and the wasmtime-wasi rows produce no Dependabot alert at all, because a crates.io
# advisory inside a pip wheel is not a manifest Dependabot reads.
# Alert counts and register rows are different units; neither number is the other's check.

# Eight npm advisories left this file on 2026-10-14, because they stopped being true: the
# lockfile lane applied the overrides the blocks below used to ask for, and Dependabot reports
# all eight closed (katex 0.18.2, source-map-js 1.2.2, brace-expansion 1.1.21 and 5.0.12).
# A fixed row leaves the register: an allowance nobody needs is an allowance for whoever
# recreates the package.
# Measured after the overrides landed — `pnpm audit --prod` and `pnpm audit`: 0 records each.
# Why it is fixed: the eight npm advisories that left this file on 2026-10-14 came back as
# `state=fixed`, and the
# reason is the gate's own rule rather than tidiness: `test_a_pnpm_advisory_is_judged_against_the_register`
# requires that an advisory the register carries is decided, so that a dev-only decision stays a
# decision. Removing the rows entirely made a real advisory look undecided. A `fixed` row keeps
# `fixed_in` and carries no `blocked_by`.
# Measured the same day, after the overrides landed: `pnpm audit` and `pnpm audit --prod` both
# Exposure as measured: all eight were dev-only or lazily loaded. The two that reached a shipped
# path were measured — katex 0.16.47 arrived through `.>remark-math>micromark-extension-math` with
# `pnpm audit --prod` reporting dev=false, and it now resolves to 0.18.2.
# return **0** records, and Dependabot reports all eight closed.
# Why it is fixed — Exposure as measured: the vulnerable copies are gone from the lock; the
# two that reached a shipped path were proved (katex through remark-math with dev=false) and
# the rest were dev-only, so nothing here is exposed to a user.
GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7  # package=katex ecosystem=npm scope=runtime state=fixed affected=>=0.11.0,<0.18.2 fixed_in=0.18.2 recheck=2026-11-06
GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr  # package=brace-expansion ecosystem=npm scope=development state=fixed affected=<1.1.21|>=4.0.0,<5.0.12 fixed_in=1.1.21 recheck=2026-11-06
GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7  # package=brace-expansion ecosystem=npm scope=development state=fixed affected=<1.1.20|>=4.0.0,<5.0.11 fixed_in=1.1.20 recheck=2026-11-06
GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p  # package=brace-expansion ecosystem=npm scope=development state=fixed affected=<1.1.19|>=4.0.0,<5.0.10 fixed_in=1.1.19 recheck=2026-11-06
GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q  # package=source-map-js ecosystem=npm scope=development state=fixed affected=>=1.0.0,<1.2.2 fixed_in=1.2.2 recheck=2026-11-06

# GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g = RUSTSEC-2024-0429 — glib.
# Why it is not fixed yet: glib 0.20.0 is the fix and app/src-tauri/Cargo.lock pins 0.18.5,
# and the move waits on upstream, measured: `cargo update -p glib --precise 0.20.0` is refused —
# gtk 0.18.2 requires `glib = "^0.18"` and tauri 2.12.3 is crates.io's newest stable. The version
# chain is in wt/w7-glib's report. The coverage gap this row first recorded is closed:
# supply-chain.yml's "Cargo advisory verdict" audits app/src-tauri/Cargo.lock against the
# crates.io database (hygiene.yml still reads the lock only for Tauri plugin major/minor
# parity), and .github/dependabot.yml now declares package-ecosystem "cargo" for
# /app/src-tauri, so this alert CAN arrive as a pull request — which is why the `glib` ignore
# entry was added there. Until that landed, the row was invisible to every gate in this repo
# and Dependabot was its only reader.
# Exposure as measured: dependencies arrive through the Tauri desktop shell, which is the
# product's own window process, so this is runtime and not build tooling. Unsound Iterator
# and DoubleEndedIterator implementations for glib::VariantStrIter (CVSS:4.0 AV:N/AC:L
# PR:N/UI:N/VI:L) — a soundness defect, medium severity, no code-execution path claimed.
GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g  # package=glib ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=pending-fix affected=>=0.15.0,<0.20.0 fixed_in=0.20.0 blocked_by=tauri-pins-gtk-0.18 recheck=2026-11-06

# --- The fixed rows. A finding whose release landed, kept as the floor that holds it. ---

# GHSA-54p9-h82j-f925 = CVE-2026-104874 — multidict. The CVE record is the one with no
# package attached (its ranges are git commits), so this row cites the GitHub ID that
# osv.dev resolves against `multidict`; scripts/advisory_id_check.py reads aliases for
# exactly that reason and reports a mismatched pair rather than waving it through.
# Why it is fixed: 6.9.1 is the first fixed release, uv.lock resolves multidict 6.9.1, the
# constraint `multidict>=6.9.1` holds it, and lockfile.yml re-resolves against the pinned uv.
# Exposure as measured: reference leak in CIMultiDict/MultiDict items-view union and
# subtraction (introduced 6.7.0), read from the advisory record on 2026-10-14.
GHSA-54p9-h82j-f925  # package=multidict ecosystem=PyPI scope=runtime state=fixed affected=>=6.7.0 fixed_in=6.9.1 recheck=2026-11-06

# --- The crates.io rows found by the Cargo verdict leg. ---

# RUSTSEC-2024-0370 — proc-macro-error 1.0.4. Found 2026-10-14 by
# `python3 scripts/advisory_id_check.py --audit-cargo`, the leg added the same day: it reads
# all 512 crate(s) app/src-tauri/Cargo.lock pins and found three with an advisory record —
# glib (the row above), rustls 0.23.45 (bumped to 0.23.46 in the same commit, which closed
# eight records) and this one, the only one with nothing to move to.
# Why there is no fix: the RustSec record carries no fixed event, no CVSS and no CVE, and
# its own `database_specific.informational` field says the reason — the crate is
# unmaintained. The successors (proc-macro-error2) are a different crate, so no version
# bump reaches this; it clears when the GTK stack does.
# Exposure as measured: compile-time only. The paths in the lock are glib-macros 0.18.5 and
# gtk3-macros 0.18.2, both proc-macro crates of the GTK 0.18 stack that build the Tauri
# shell; `cargo tree -i proc-macro-error` on the host target answers "nothing to print", so
# it is not compiled into the aarch64-apple-darwin build at all, and a proc-macro emits
# code into the compiler rather than into the artifact. scope=development follows from
# that. UNPROVEN: that it is equally absent from every platform a release ships, since
# `cargo tree --target all` was not run against all targets.
RUSTSEC-2024-0370  # package=proc-macro-error ecosystem=crates.io scope=development state=accepted affected=>=0.0.0 fixed_in=none recheck=2026-11-06

# zbus_names, zvariant and zvariant_derive reached the lock with tauri-plugin-notification
# 2.7.0 on 2026-10-18 (zbus 5.19 <- notify-rust 4.18; the other two are its support
# crates and its derive). None is in the aarch64-apple-darwin build: `cargo tree -i` on
# the host answers "nothing to print" for all three, and `--target all` shows only the
# Linux D-Bus paths (notifications, single-instance activation). The Linux bundle carries
# them; the macOS and Windows surfaces do not.
# Why there is no fix: all three are RustSec "unmaintained" records with no fixed event
# and no successor crate to move to, so no release exists to pin.
# Exposure as measured: D-Bus names and serialized values on Linux, in the notification
# and single-instance plugins. They do not parse the product's own payloads; the records
# describe missing maintenance with no reachable defect. Re-read with the next notification
# plugin bump, which is when the zbus family moves.
RUSTSEC-2026-0371  # package=zbus_names ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=accepted affected=>=0.0.0 fixed_in=none recheck=2026-11-06
RUSTSEC-2026-0370  # package=zvariant ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=accepted affected=>=0.0.0 fixed_in=none recheck=2026-11-06
RUSTSEC-2026-0372  # package=zvariant_derive ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=accepted affected=>=0.0.0 fixed_in=none recheck=2026-11-06

# zip 4.6.1 came in as tauri-plugin-updater 2.14.0's own dependency. The three
# findings carry a RustSec ID and a GHSA alias each: SUID/SGID preservation during
# extraction, symlink targets outside the destination, and permissions applied through
# those symlinks. Every one of them closes with zip 9.0.0. The rows below name the
# RustSec IDs: GitHub serves no advisory page for the GHSA aliases (HTTP 404 on
# 2026-10-18), while OSV resolves each alias to the RustSec record it shares.
# Why it is not fixed yet: the updater's manifest pins the 4.x line, so the lock cannot
# move to 9.0.0 without the plugin moving first; that is upstream's open work.
# Exposure as measured: `cargo tree -i zip` on the host target prints nothing, so the
# macOS build does not carry it; the Linux updater does, and it extracts the release
# archive it has just verified against the signature in latest.json. The attack needs a
# crafted archive that passes that signature; a hostile network response alone does not.
RUSTSEC-2026-0367  # package=zip ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=pending-fix affected=>=0.0.0,<9.0.0 fixed_in=9.0.0 blocked_by=tauri-plugin-updater-pins-zip-4 recheck=2026-11-06
RUSTSEC-2026-0368  # package=zip ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=pending-fix affected=>=0.0.0,<9.0.0 fixed_in=9.0.0 blocked_by=tauri-plugin-updater-pins-zip-4 recheck=2026-11-06
RUSTSEC-2026-0369  # package=zip ecosystem=crates.io scope=runtime state=pending-fix affected=>=0.0.0,<9.0.0 fixed_in=9.0.0 blocked_by=tauri-plugin-updater-pins-zip-4 recheck=2026-11-06

# Re-check protocol for the npm and crates.io rows:
#   1. Re-run the gate's own commands in app/ (`pnpm audit --prod --json`, `pnpm audit
#      --json`) after any lockfile change, and the three resolver modes for the IDs and the
#      crate set: `scripts/advisory_id_check.py`, `--audit-cargo`, `--pip-verdict`.
#   2. A row moves to `state=fixed` when the bump lands and the audit stops reporting it,
#      and it stays here with `fixed_in=` naming the version the lock must hold — deleting
#      it would leave the floor in pyproject.toml or in a test with nothing pointing at it.
#      Measured 2026-10-14: rustls 0.23.45 was in this class with no row at all until the
#      cargo leg existed, and the eight records behind it were invisible to every gate.
#   3. A row that is still `pending-fix` at its recheck date keeps its line and moves the
#      date with a written reason, the same rule the Python entries above follow.
# No install and no lockfile rewrite was run in this wave; `pnpm audit` is read-only and
# app/pnpm-lock.yaml is byte-identical to the commit this was measured against.
